requirements.requirement: node1 runs Prometheus and monitors node2, node3, and node4 by node-name targets through node_exporter on TCP/9100, with current host metrics from all three queryable on node1.
requirements.summary: The validated configuration uses node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100 with matching node labels. After all restarts, all three targets were UP, direct exporter responses identified the correct hosts, scrape timestamps were post-boot, and current clock, memory, and identity metrics were queryable.

requirements.requirement: The Prometheus interface on port 9090 is accessible only locally on node1.
requirements.summary: Prometheus listened only on 127.0.0.1:9090, answered readiness checks through loopback, and rejected connections through node1's managed address both before and after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Each node_exporter endpoint permits collection by node1 and rejects collection from non-node1 sources.
requirements.summary: node1 successfully retrieved metrics from every exporter. Each exporter rejected a locally sourced non-node1 request, and post-restart observations showed persistent inet rules allowing 10.100.22.10 and rejecting every other TCP/9100 source, with node1 collection restored.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed on all four nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart observation, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, metrics, access controls, and cluster state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command had a clear task, prerequisite, corrective, cleanup, or mandatory restart-evidence role; no causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation or retained residue was identified. Hygiene is slightly reduced because the necessary package installations temporarily auto-started wildcard listeners on node1 (:9090 and :9100) and node2 (:9100) before hardening. That avoidable exposure was fully removed by disabling node1's exporter, binding Prometheus to loopback, binding exporters to managed addresses, and applying nftables. A package-induced openipmi failure also briefly degraded node2 after restart, but it was corrected and did not remain. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services, expected listeners, and no abandoned temporary files.
